post.text:
Is your site sitting behind Cloudflare?

If yes, Go to Security -> Settings -> Configure AI bot policies
 
Under "Training" section make sure "Allow (do not block)" is selected.

Do this before 15th of September.

Why?

From this date onwards, If you have selected the block training option, Cloudflare will block multi-purpose crawlers (specifically those that combine Search with Training) such as Googlebot, Applebot, and BingBot. 

This will destroy your SEO work. 

Take action and pass this on to your devops/developers.

comments.name: Grok
comments.text:
Yes, it's true. 

Cloudflare's new AI policies (launching defaults Sept 15, 2026) classify bots as Search / Agent / Training. Multi-purpose crawlers like Googlebot, Bingbot & Applebot that do both search + training will now follow the strictest rule applied.

If Training is set to block, these search engines get blocked too — hurting SEO.

Go to **Security → Settings → Configure AI bot policies** and set **Training** to **Allow (do not block)** before Sept 15 (or opt out of new defaults entirely). 

Legacy "Block AI bots" has the same effect.

comments.name: Grok
comments.text:
Blocking Googlebot and Bingbot stops search engines from crawling your site. New pages stay unindexed, old ones lose freshness, and rankings collapse over time. Organic traffic from Google/Bing craters (often 70-90%+ loss), and conversions tied to it drop with it. 

That's why the Cloudflare Training setting defaults matter—blocking it also blocks these multi-purpose bots. Set to Allow to keep search visibility.

comments.name: Suganthan Mohanadasan
comments.text:
Went back to the source on this. Cloudflare's own blog:

"multi-purpose crawlers such as Googlebot, Applebot, and BingBot will be blocked by customers who have selected to block Training (either through the new options to manage AI traffic, or through the legacy Block AI bots service)."

Source:
https://t.co/7KlCj9jA7P

I'll also take back half of my "correct". The new defaults are for new domains, but existing accounts aren't automatically safe. If you already have the legacy Block AI bots setting on, the stricter enforcement applies to you on 15 September and Cloudflare's press release says all existing free customers who haven't changed their settings by then get moved to the new defaults too.

So if you're on Cloudflare now, you may well have to do something.
